finding: V15 verdict is hard coded as partial although its registered refutation clause ('at or below 100 percent') is met: the drone stream utilisation is 0.43, and robot on 802.15.4 is 0.86.
evidence: mission/results/base.csv: drone C sik utilisation_median 0.429, robot C ieee802154 0.859; scorer line 82 assigns the string 'partial' without computing a verdict; 'partial' is not defined for V15 in PREDICTIONS_V4.md.

finding: V21 is scored hit by verdict(True); the computed frame lr is never used. On LoRaWAN DR0 the hybrid handshake never completes (ttra NaN), so recovery time is undefined; on the SiK radio, the slowest link that carries commands, it is 0.92 s, below the 1 s prediction, which would refute it. ttra here equals the first session time, not recovery after link loss.
evidence: base.csv: drone B lora_dr0 ttra_s_median NaN; drone B sik ttra_s_median 0.916 = first_session_s_median 0.916; PROTOCOL_SIM.md line 12 gives 1.36 s for the hybrid mavlink2_pq handshake on SiK, so the verdict also depends on which model is chosen.
suggested_fix: Compute V21 from a recovery metric; state which link is 'slowest robotics link' as registered; score not scored or miss rather than hard coding hit.

line_or_section: checks.py lines 30 to 43; scorer lines 77 to 78; SCORES V14
finding: V14 ('does the loss model agree with closed forms') is scored hit on a purpose written geometric sampler (sw_transmissions_data_loss) that cannot disagree with 1/(1-p); the simulator's own stop and wait is relabelled 'supplementary', sits above its closed form at all 5 loss rates and misses once. The protocol and mission results use selective repeat, which has no closed form check.

suggested_fix: Score V14 on the simulator that produces results (sim.stop_and_wait or selective repeat); report the systematic upward bias; remove the tautological check from the verdict.

line_or_section: validate_v4.py lines 98 to 104; scorer line 66; PAPER line 68
finding: LoRa time on air 'validation' is circular: for C1.4 and C1.6 the unstated CRC, header and DE settings were chosen because they 'reproduce it'; C2.3 assumes CR and preamble. finding: V10 cannot be refuted as executed: its refutation clause is 'battery capacity has the largest first order index', but battery capacity is not an input of the Sobol analysis. The indices are also for the ML-DSA-44 per command design, not the session workload named in V9 and V10.

finding: Headline overgeneralises the cycle model: 'validated on published rows it was not fitted to' and 'from validated model to hardware' without the caveat that every test binary has a sibling parameter set of the same implementation in training; 12 free costs fitted to 27 rows from 9 binaries give implausible costs, so 1.0 percent measures interpolation, not prediction.

finding: Method claims every model is validated on data it was not fitted to, with the error reported before any modelled value is used. Mission shares, the mission simulation, the planner and the exposure model have no validation data; the boot check is 3 rows. The same paragraph says the a priori model uses 'the timing tables of the core', which were never retrieved.

suggested_fix: State per model whether it is validated, calibrated only, or unvalidated; replace 'timing tables of the core' with 'assumed per class costs'.

line_or_section: run_all.py lines 190 to 225; SCORES V8; PAPER line 64

finding: Handshake 'validation' fits an additive constant on 2 rows of ePrint 2026/2343 Table 5 and tests on 3 rows of the same table and testbed; the near zero test error reflects the shared setup, not model skill (uncalibrated errors -29 to -43 percent). finding: The table's '95% CI' (for example '1.87 [1.87, 1.87]') covers only Monte Carlo noise around fixed assumptions, not input uncertainty. Feasibility of B on IEEE 802.15.4 rests on the link model the study itself finds 4.2 times too fast, with B on SiK at 0.9915 [0.9908, 0.9922] just above the assumed 0.99 threshold.

suggested_fix: Rename to Monte Carlo interval; flag 802.15.4 verdicts as conditional on an unvalidated link model; show a sensitivity of the verdicts to the 802.15.4 time factor.

finding: H1 tests 95 percent intervals with a refutation at 'more than a third outside', which is lenient. Board errors are strongly correlated (one board, wait states against the zero wait state assumption), so the outcome is close to all or nothing. H2 predicts within 2 s but refutes only above 5 s, so 2 to 5 s gives no verdict.
evidence: PREDICTIONS_V4_BOARD.md conditions 'zero flash wait states, no cache'; H2 row.
suggested_fix: Refute H1 when the outside share is clearly above 5 percent (for example above 20 percent), and analyse the systematic offset separately; close the H2 gap.

finding: A 'partial' verdict, used for the zone between prediction and refutation, is not defined in PREDICTIONS_V4.md or PROTOCOL_V4.md; the totals line (17 hit, 1 partial, 3 miss) mixes a post hoc category with registered ones.
evidence: grep of PROTOCOL_V4.md and PREDICTIONS_V4.md for 'partial' finds nothing.
